verses.zh: 亚伯拉罕年纪老迈，向来在一切事上耶和华都赐福给他。
verses.en: Now Abraham was old, well advanced in years,[NOTE:1] and the Lord had blessed him[NOTE:2] in everything.
notes: Heb “days.”
Heb “Abraham.” The proper name has been replaced in the translation by the pronoun (“he”) for stylistic reasons.

verses.zh: 亚伯拉罕对管理他全业最老的仆人说：「请你把手放在我大腿底下。
verses.en: Abraham said to his servant, the senior one[NOTE:1] in his household who was in charge of everything he had, “Put your hand under my thigh[NOTE:2]
notes: The Hebrew term זָקֵן (zaqen) may refer to the servant who is oldest in age or senior in authority (or both).

Put your hand under my thigh. The taking of this oath had to do with the sanctity of the family and the continuation of the family line. See D. R. Freedman, “Put Your Hand Under My Thigh—the Patriarchal Oath,” BAR 2 (1976): 2-4, 42.

verses.zh: 我要叫你指着耶和华―天地的主起誓，不要为我儿子娶这迦南地中的女子为妻。
verses.en: so that I may make you solemnly promise[NOTE:1] by the Lord, the God of heaven and the God of the earth: You must not acquire[NOTE:2] a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites, among whom I am living.
notes: Following the imperative, the cohortative with the prefixed conjunction indicates purpose.
Heb “because you must not take.”

verses.zh: 你要往我本地本族去，为我的儿子以撒娶一个妻子。」
verses.en: You must go instead to my country and to my relatives[NOTE:1] to find[NOTE:2] a wife for my son Isaac.”
notes: Heb “for to my country and my relatives you must go.”
Heb “and take.”

verses.zh: 仆人对他说：「倘若女子不肯跟我到这地方来，我必须将你的儿子带回你原出之地吗？」
verses.en: The servant asked him, “What if the woman is not willing to come back with me[NOTE:1] to this land? Must I then[NOTE:2] take your son back to the land from which you came?”
notes: Heb “to go after me.”
In the Hebrew text the construction is emphatic; the infinitive absolute precedes the imperfect. However, it is difficult to reflect this emphasis in an English translation.

verses.zh: 亚伯拉罕对他说：「你要谨慎，不要带我的儿子回那里去。
verses.en: “Be careful[NOTE:1] never to take my son back there!” Abraham told him.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “guard yourself.”
The introductory clause “And Abraham said to him” has been moved to the end of the opening sentence of direct discourse in the translation for stylistic reasons.

verses.zh: 耶和华―天上的主曾带领我离开父家和本族的地，对我说话，向我起誓说：『我要将这地赐给你的后裔。』他必差遣使者在你面前，你就可以从那里为我儿子娶一个妻子。
verses.en: “The Lord, the God of heaven, who took me from my father’s house and the land of my relatives,[NOTE:1] promised me with a solemn oath,[NOTE:2] ‘To your descendants I will give this land.’ He will send his angel[NOTE:3] before you so that you may find[NOTE:4] a wife for my son from there.
notes: Or “the land of my birth.”
Heb “and who spoke to me and who swore to me, saying.”
Or “his messenger.”
Heb “before you and you will take.”

verses.zh: 倘若女子不肯跟你来，我使你起的誓就与你无干了，只是不可带我的儿子回那里去。」
verses.en: But if the woman is not willing to come back with you,[NOTE:1] you will be free[NOTE:2] from this oath of mine. But you must not take my son back there!”
notes: Heb “ to go after you.”
You will be free. If the prospective bride was not willing to accompany the servant back to Canaan, the servant would be released from his oath to Abraham.

verses.zh: 仆人就把手放在他主人亚伯拉罕的大腿底下，为这事向他起誓。
verses.en: So the servant placed his hand under the thigh of his master Abraham and gave his solemn promise he would carry out his wishes.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and he swore to him concerning this matter.”

verses.zh: 那仆人从他主人的骆驼里取了十匹骆驼，并带些他主人各样的财物，起身往美索不达米亚去，到了拿鹤的城。
verses.en: Then the servant took ten of his master’s camels and departed with all kinds of gifts from his master at his disposal.[NOTE:1] He journeyed[NOTE:2] to the region of Aram Naharaim[NOTE:3] and the city of Nahor.
notes: Heb “and every good thing of his master was in his hand.” The disjunctive clause is circumstantial, explaining that he took all kinds of gifts to be used at his discretion.
Heb “and he arose and went.”
Aram Naharaim means in Hebrew “Aram of the Two Rivers,” a region in northern Mesopotamia.tn The words “the region of” are not in the Hebrew text, but are supplied in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 天将晚，众女子出来打水的时候，他便叫骆驼跪在城外的水井那里。
verses.en: He made the camels kneel down by the well[NOTE:1] outside the city. It was evening,[NOTE:2] the time when the women would go out to draw water.
notes: Heb “well of water.”
Heb “at the time of evening.”

verses.zh: 他说：「耶和华―我主人亚伯拉罕的　神啊，求你施恩给我主人亚伯拉罕，使我今日遇见好机会。
verses.en: He prayed, “O Lord, God of my master Abraham, guide me today.[NOTE:1] Be faithful[NOTE:2] to my master Abraham.
notes: Heb “make it happen before me today.” Although a number of English translations understand this as a request for success in the task (cf. NASB, NIV, NRSV) it is more likely that the servant is requesting an omen or sign from God (v. 14).
Heb “act in loyal love with” or “show kindness to.”

verses.zh: 我现今站在井旁，城内居民的女子们正出来打水。
verses.en: Here I am, standing by the spring,[NOTE:1] and the daughters of the people[NOTE:2] who live in the town are coming out to draw water.
notes: Heb “the spring of water.”
Heb “the men.”

verses.zh: 我向那一个女子说：『请你拿下水瓶来，给我水喝。』她若说：『请喝！我也给你的骆驼喝。』愿那女子就作你所预定给你仆人以撒的妻。这样，我便知道你施恩给我主人了。」
verses.en: I will say to a young woman, ‘Please lower your jar so I may drink.’ May the one you have chosen for your servant Isaac reply, ‘Drink, and I’ll give your camels water too.’[NOTE:1] In this way I will know that you have been faithful to my master.”[NOTE:2]
notes: I will also give your camels water. It would be an enormous test for a young woman to water ten camels. The idea is that such a woman would not only be industrious but hospitable and generous.

Heb “And let the young woman to whom I say, ‘Lower your jar that I may drink,’ and she says, ‘Drink and I will also give your camels water,’—her you have appointed for your servant, for Isaac, and by it I will know that you have acted in faithfulness with my master.”

verses.zh: 话还没有说完，不料，利百加肩头上扛着水瓶出来。利百加是彼土利所生的；彼土利是亚伯拉罕兄弟拿鹤妻子密迦的儿子。
verses.en: Before he had finished praying, there came Rebekah[NOTE:1] with her water jug on her shoulder. She was the daughter of Bethuel son of Milcah (Milcah was the wife of Abraham’s brother Nahor).[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “Look, Rebekah was coming out!” Using the participle introduced with הִנֵּה (hinneh, “look”), the narrator dramatically transports the audience back into the event and invites them to see Rebekah through the servant’s eyes.

Heb “Look, Rebekah was coming out—[she] who was born to Bethuel, the son of Milcah, the wife of Nahor, the brother of Abraham—and her jug [was] on her shoulder.” The order of the clauses has been rearranged in the translation for stylistic reasons.

verses.zh: 那女子容貌极其俊美，还是处女，也未曾有人亲近她。她下到井旁，打满了瓶，又上来。
verses.en: Now the young woman was very beautiful. She was a virgin; no man had ever been physically intimate with her.[NOTE:1] She went down to the spring, filled her jug, and came back up.
notes: Heb “And the young woman was very good of appearance, a virgin, and a man had not known her.” The first two terms נַעֲרָה (naʿarah) and בְּתוּלָה (betulah) can refer to young girls, either unmarried or married; see Judges 9:3 and Joel 1:8, respectively, for examples of a married נַעֲרָה (naʿarah) and בְּתוּלָה (betulah). While the term בְּתוּלָה (betulah) does not have to mean “virgin” it can refer to a girl who is a virgin. Further, in legal literature it is used as a technical term for “virgin” (Exod 22:16-17; Deut 22:19, 23, 28). Akkadian behaves similarly in that the cognate term batultu, meaning an adolescent girl but not necessarily a “virgin,” is used to mean “virgin” in Neo-Assyrian laws and Neo-Babylonian marriage contracts (CAD B 173-174). This passage is not legal literature, so the meaning “virgin” is clarified by an additional clause. The expression “to know” is a euphemism for sexual relations, and the English euphemism “be intimate with” is close in meaning to the Hebrew. The Semitic languages may have lacked a term that specifically meant “virgin” and so promoted other terms to indicate a virgin, whether by the context of the type of literature (e.g. legal literature) or by the addition of explanatory clauses.

verses.zh: 仆人跑上前去迎着她，说：「求你将瓶里的水给我一点喝。」
verses.en: Abraham’s servant[NOTE:1] ran to meet her and said, “Please give me a sip of water from your jug.”
notes: Heb “and the servant.” The word “Abraham’s” has been supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.

verses.zh: 女子说：「我主请喝！」就急忙拿下瓶来，托在手上给他喝。
verses.en: “Drink, my lord,” she replied, and quickly lowering[NOTE:1] her jug to her hands, she gave him a drink.
notes: Heb “and she hurried and lowered.”

verses.zh: 女子给他喝了，就说：「我再为你的骆驼打水，叫骆驼也喝足。」
verses.en: When she had done so,[NOTE:1] she said, “I’ll draw water for your camels too, until they have drunk as much as they want.”
notes: Heb “when she had finished giving him a drink.” This has been simplified in the translation for stylistic reasons.

verses.zh: 她就急忙把瓶里的水倒在槽里，又跑到井旁打水，就为所有的骆驼打上水来。
verses.en: She quickly emptied[NOTE:1] her jug into the watering trough and ran back to the well to draw more water until she had drawn enough for all his camels.
notes: Heb “and she hurried and emptied.”

verses.zh: 那人定睛看她，一句话也不说，要晓得耶和华赐他通达的道路没有。
verses.en: Silently the man watched her with interest to determine[NOTE:1] if the Lord had made his journey successful[NOTE:2] or not.
notes: Heb “to know.”
The Hebrew term צָלָה (tsalah), meaning “to make successful” in the Hiphil verbal stem, is a key term in the story (see vv. 40, 42, 56).

verses.zh: 骆驼喝足了，那人就拿一个金环，重半舍客勒，两个金镯，重十舍客勒，给了那女子，
verses.en: After the camels had finished drinking, the man took out a gold nose ring weighing a beka[NOTE:1] and two gold wrist bracelets weighing ten shekels[NOTE:2] and gave them to her.[NOTE:3]
notes: A beka weighed about 5-6 grams (0.2 ounce).
A shekel weighed about 11.5 grams (0.4 ounce) although weights varied locally, so these bracelets weighed about 4 ounces (115 grams).
The words “and gave them to her” are not in the Hebrew text, but are implied (cf. Gen 24:30).

verses.zh: 说：「请告诉我，你是谁的女儿？你父亲家里有我们住宿的地方没有？」
verses.en: “Whose daughter are you?” he asked.[NOTE:1] “Tell me, is there room in your father’s house for us to spend the night?”
notes: Heb “and he said, ‘Whose daughter are you?’” The order of the introductory clause has been rearranged in the translation for stylistic reasons.

verses.zh: 女子说：「我是密迦与拿鹤之子彼土利的女儿」；
verses.en: She said to him, “I am the daughter of Bethuel the son of Milcah, whom Milcah bore to Nahor.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “whom she bore to Nahor.” The referent (Milcah) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 又说：「我们家里足有粮草，也有住宿的地方。」
verses.en: We have plenty of straw and feed,” she added,[NOTE:1] “and room for you[NOTE:2] to spend the night.”
notes: Heb “and she said, ‘We have plenty of both straw and feed.’” The order of the introductory clause has been rearranged in the translation for stylistic reasons.
Heb The words “for you” are not in the Hebrew text, but are implied.

verses.zh: 那人就低头向耶和华下拜，
verses.en: The man bowed his head and worshiped the Lord,

verses.zh: 说：「耶和华―我主人亚伯拉罕的　神是应当称颂的，因他不断地以慈爱诚实待我主人。至于我，耶和华在路上引领我，直走到我主人的兄弟家里。」
verses.en: saying, “Praised be the Lord, the God of my master Abraham, who has not abandoned his faithful love[NOTE:1] for my master! The Lord has led me[NOTE:2] to the house[NOTE:3] of my master’s relatives!”[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “his faithfulness and his commitment.”
Heb “As for me—in the way the Lord led me.”
Here “house” is an adverbial accusative of termination.
Heb “brothers.”

verses.zh: 女子跑回去，照着这些话告诉她母亲和她家里的人。
verses.en: The young woman ran and told her mother’s household all about[NOTE:1] these things.
notes: Heb “according to.”

verses.zh: 利百加有一个哥哥，名叫拉班，看见金环，又看见金镯在他妹子的手上，并听见他妹子利百加的话，说那人对我如此如此说。拉班就跑出来往井旁去，到那人跟前，见他仍站在骆驼旁边的井旁那里，
verses.en: (Now Rebekah had a brother named Laban.)[NOTE:1] Laban rushed out to meet the man at the spring.
notes: The parenthetical disjunctive clause introduces the audience to Laban, who will eventually play an important role in the unfolding story.

verses.zh: 并入上节
verses.en: When he saw the bracelets on his sister’s wrists and the nose ring[NOTE:1] and heard his sister Rebekah say,[NOTE:2] “This is what the man said to me,” he went out to meet the man. There he was, standing[NOTE:3] by the camels near the spring.
notes: Heb “And it was when he saw the nose ring and the bracelets on the arms of his sister.” The word order is altered in the translation for the sake of clarity.
Heb “and when he heard the words of Rebekah his sister, saying.”
Heb “and look, he was standing.” The disjunctive clause with the participle following the particle הִנֵּה (hinneh) invites the audience to view the scene through Laban’s eyes.

verses.zh: 便对他说：「你这蒙耶和华赐福的，请进来，为甚么站在外边？我已经收拾了房屋，也为骆驼预备了地方。」
verses.en: Laban said to him,[NOTE:1] “Come, you who are blessed by the Lord![NOTE:2] Why are you standing out here when I have prepared[NOTE:3] the house and a place for the camels?”
notes: Heb “and he said.” The referent (Laban) has been specified and the words “to him” supplied in the translation for clarity.

Laban’s obsession with wealth is apparent; to him it represents how one is blessed by the Lord. Already the author is laying the foundation for subsequent events in the narrative, where Laban’s greed becomes his dominant characteristic.
The disjunctive clause is circumstantial.

verses.zh: 那人就进了拉班的家。拉班卸了骆驼，用草料喂上，拿水给那人和跟随的人洗脚；
verses.en: So Abraham’s servant[NOTE:1] went to the house and unloaded[NOTE:2] the camels. Straw and feed were given[NOTE:3] to the camels, and water was provided so that he and the men who were with him could wash their feet.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “the man”; the referent (Abraham’s servant) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

Some translations (e.g., NEB, NASB, NRSV) understand Laban to be the subject of this and the following verbs or take the subject of this and the following verbs as indefinite (referring to an unnamed servant; e.g., NAB, NIV).
Heb “and [one] gave.” The verb without an expressed subject may be translated as passive.
Heb “and water to wash his feet and the feet of the men who were with him.”

verses.zh: 把饭摆在他面前，叫他吃，他却说：「我不吃，等我说明白我的事情再吃。」拉班说：「请说。」
verses.en: When food was served,[NOTE:1] he said, “I will not eat until I have said what I want to say.”[NOTE:2] “Tell us,” Laban said.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “and food was placed before him.”
Heb “my words.”
Heb “and he said, ‘Speak.’” The referent (Laban) has been specified in the translation for clarity.tc Some ancient textual witnesses have a plural verb, “and they said.”

verses.zh: 他说：「我是亚伯拉罕的仆人。
verses.en: “I am the servant of Abraham,” he began.

verses.zh: 耶和华大大地赐福给我主人，使他昌大，又赐给他羊群、牛群、金银、仆婢、骆驼，和驴。
verses.en: “The Lord has richly blessed my master and he has become very wealthy.[NOTE:1] The Lord[NOTE:2] has given him sheep and cattle, silver and gold, male and female servants, and camels and donkeys.
notes: Heb “become great.” In this context the statement refers primarily to Abraham’s material wealth, although reputation and influence are not excluded.
Heb “and he.” The referent (the Lord) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 我主人的妻子撒拉年老的时候给我主人生了一个儿子；我主人也将一切所有的都给了这个儿子。
verses.en: My master’s wife Sarah bore a son to him[NOTE:1] when she was old,[NOTE:2] and my master[NOTE:3] has given him everything he owns.
notes: Heb “to my master.” This has been replaced by the pronoun “him” in the translation for stylistic reasons.
Heb “after her old age.”
Heb “and he.” The referent (the servant’s master, Abraham) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 我主人叫我起誓说：『你不要为我儿子娶迦南地的女子为妻。
verses.en: My master made me swear an oath. He said, ‘You must not acquire a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites, among whom I am living,

verses.zh: 你要往我父家、我本族那里去，为我的儿子娶一个妻子。』
verses.en: but you must go to the family of my father and to my relatives to find[NOTE:1] a wife for my son.’
notes: Heb “but to the house of my father you must go and to my family and you must take a wife for my son.”

verses.zh: 我对我主人说：『恐怕女子不肯跟我来。』
verses.en: But I said to my master, ‘What if the woman does not want to go[NOTE:1] with me?’[NOTE:2]
notes: The imperfect is used here in a modal sense to indicate desire.
Heb “after me.”

verses.zh: 他就说：『我所事奉的耶和华必要差遣他的使者与你同去，叫你的道路通达，你就得以在我父家、我本族那里，给我的儿子娶一个妻子。
verses.en: He answered, ‘The Lord, before whom I have walked,[NOTE:1] will send his angel with you. He will make your journey a success and you will find a wife for my son from among my relatives, from my father’s family.
notes: The verb is the Hitpael of הָלַךְ (halakh), meaning “live one’s life” (see Gen 17:1). The statement may simply refer to serving the Lord or it may have a more positive moral connotation (“serve faithfully”).

verses.zh: 只要你到了我本族那里，我使你起的誓就与你无干。他们若不把女子交给你，我使你起的誓也与你无干。』
verses.en: You will be free from your oath[NOTE:1] if you go to my relatives and they will not give her to you. Then you will be free from your oath.’
notes: Heb “my oath” (twice in this verse). From the Hebrew perspective the oath belonged to the person to whom it was sworn (Abraham), although in contemporary English an oath is typically viewed as belonging to the person who swears it (the servant).

verses.zh: 「我今日到了井旁，便说：『耶和华―我主人亚伯拉罕的　神啊，愿你叫我所行的道路通达。
verses.en: When I came to the spring today, I prayed, ‘O Lord, God of my master Abraham, if you have decided to make my journey successful,[NOTE:1] may events unfold as follows:[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “if you are making successful my way on which I am going.”
The words “may events unfold as follows” are supplied in the translation for clarification and for stylistic reasons.

verses.zh: 我如今站在井旁，对哪一个出来打水的女子说：请你把你瓶里的水给我一点喝；
verses.en: Here I am, standing by the spring.[NOTE:1] When[NOTE:2] the young woman goes out to draw water, I’ll say, “Please give me a little water to drink from your jug.”
notes: Heb “the spring of water.”
Heb “and it will be.”

verses.zh: 她若说：你只管喝，我也为你的骆驼打水；愿那女子就作耶和华给我主人儿子所预定的妻。』
verses.en: Then she will reply to me, “Drink, and I’ll draw water for your camels too.” May that woman be the one whom the Lord has chosen for my master’s son.’

verses.zh: 我心里的话还没有说完，利百加就出来，肩头上扛着水瓶，下到井旁打水。我便对她说：『请你给我水喝。』
verses.en: “Before I finished praying in my heart,[NOTE:1] along came Rebekah[NOTE:2] with her water jug on her shoulder! She went down to the spring and drew water. So I said to her, ‘Please give me a drink.’
notes: Heb “As for me, before I finished speaking to my heart.” The adverb טֶרֶם (terem) indicates the verb is a preterite; the infinitive that follows is the direct object.
Heb “Look, Rebekah was coming out.” As in 24:15, the particle הִנֵּה (hinneh, “look”) is used here for dramatic effect.

verses.zh: 她就急忙从肩头上拿下瓶来，说：『请喝！我也给你的骆驼喝。』我便喝了；她又给我的骆驼喝了。
verses.en: She quickly lowered her jug from her shoulder and said, ‘Drink, and I’ll give your camels water too.’ So I drank, and she also gave the camels water.

verses.zh: 我问她说：『你是谁的女儿？』她说：『我是密迦与拿鹤之子彼土利的女儿。』我就把环子戴在她鼻子上，把镯子戴在她两手上。
verses.en: Then I asked her, ‘Whose daughter are you?’ She replied, ‘The daughter of Bethuel the son of Nahor, whom Milcah bore to Nahor.’[NOTE:1] I put the ring in her nose and the bracelets on her wrists.
notes: Heb “whom Milcah bore to him.” The referent (Nahor) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 随后我低头向耶和华下拜，称颂耶和华―我主人亚伯拉罕的　神；因为他引导我走合适的道路，使我得着我主人兄弟的孙女，给我主人的儿子为妻。
verses.en: Then I bowed down and worshiped the Lord. I praised the Lord, the God of my master Abraham, who had led me on the right path to find the granddaughter[NOTE:1] of my master’s brother for his son.
notes: Heb “daughter.” Rebekah was actually the granddaughter of Nahor, Abraham’s brother. One can either translate the Hebrew term בַּת (bat) as “daughter,” in which case the term אָח (ʾakh) must be translated more generally as “relative” rather than “brother” (cf. NASB, NRSV) or one can translate בַּת as “granddaughter,” in which case אָח may be translated “brother” (cf. NIV).

verses.zh: 现在你们若愿以慈爱诚实待我主人，就告诉我；若不然，也告诉我，使我可以或向左，或向右。」
verses.en: Now, if you will show faithful love to my master, tell me. But if not, tell me as well, so that I may go on my way.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and I will turn to the right or to the left.” The expression apparently means that Abraham’s servant will know where he should go if there is no further business here.

verses.zh: 拉班和彼土利回答说：「这事乃出于耶和华，我们不能向你说好说歹。
verses.en: Then Laban and Bethuel replied, “This is the Lord’s doing.[NOTE:1] Our wishes are of no concern.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “From the Lord the matter has gone out.”
Heb “We are not able to speak to you bad or good.” This means that Laban and Bethuel could not say one way or the other what they wanted, for they viewed it as God’s will.

verses.zh: 看哪，利百加在你面前，可以将她带去，照着耶和华所说的，给你主人的儿子为妻。」
verses.en: Rebekah stands here before you. Take her and go so that she may become[NOTE:1] the wife of your master’s son, just as the Lord has decided.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Following the imperatives, the jussive with the prefixed conjunction indicates purpose or result.
Heb “as the Lord has spoken.”

verses.zh: 亚伯拉罕的仆人听见他们这话，就向耶和华俯伏在地。
verses.en: When Abraham’s servant heard their words, he bowed down to the ground before the Lord.

verses.zh: 当下仆人拿出金器、银器，和衣服送给利百加，又将宝物送给她哥哥和她母亲。
verses.en: Then he[NOTE:1] brought out gold, silver jewelry, and clothing and gave them to Rebekah. He also gave valuable gifts to her brother and to her mother.
notes: Heb “the servant”; the noun has been replaced by the pronoun (“he”) in the translation for stylistic reasons.

verses.zh: 仆人和跟从他的人吃了喝了，住了一夜。早晨起来，仆人就说：「请打发我回我主人那里去吧。」
verses.en: After this, he and the men who were with him ate a meal and stayed there overnight.[NOTE:1] When they got up in the morning, he said, “Let me leave now so I can return to my master.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “And they ate and drank, he and the men who [were] with him and they spent the night.”
Heb “Send me away to my master.”

verses.zh: 利百加的哥哥和她母亲说：「让女子同我们再住几天，至少十天，然后她可以去。」
verses.en: But Rebekah’s[NOTE:1] brother and her mother replied, “Let the girl stay with us a few more days, perhaps ten. Then she can go.”
notes: Heb “her”; the referent (Rebekah) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 仆人说：「耶和华既赐给我通达的道路，你们不要耽误我，请打发我走，回我主人那里去吧。」
verses.en: But he said to them, “Don’t detain me—the Lord[NOTE:1] has granted me success on my journey. Let me leave now so I may return[NOTE:2] to my master.”
notes: The disjunctive clause is circumstantial, indicating a reason for the preceding request.
After the preceding imperative, the cohortative with the prefixed conjunction indicates purpose or result.

verses.zh: 他们说：「我们把女子叫来问问她」，
verses.en: Then they said, “We’ll call the girl and find out what she wants to do.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and we will ask her mouth.”

verses.zh: 就叫了利百加来，问她说：「你和这人同去吗？」利百加说：「我去。」
verses.en: So they called Rebekah and asked her, “Do you want[NOTE:1] to go with this man?” She replied, “I want to go.”
notes: The imperfect verbal form here has a modal nuance, expressing desire.

verses.zh: 于是他们打发妹子利百加和她的乳母，同亚伯拉罕的仆人，并跟从仆人的，都走了。
verses.en: So they sent their sister Rebekah on her way, accompanied by her female attendant, with Abraham’s servant and his men.

verses.zh: 他们就给利百加祝福说：我们的妹子啊，愿你作千万人的母！愿你的后裔得着仇敌的城门！
verses.en: They blessed Rebekah with these words:[NOTE:1] “Our sister, may you become the mother[NOTE:2] of thousands of ten thousands! May your descendants possess the strongholds[NOTE:3] of their enemies.”
notes: Heb “and said to her.”

May you become the mother of thousands of ten thousands. The blessing expresses their prayer that she produce children and start a family line that will greatly increase (cf. Gen 17:16).tn Heb “become thousands of ten thousands.”

Heb “gate,” which here stands for a walled city. In an ancient Near Eastern city the gate complex was the main area of defense (hence the translation “stronghold”). A similar phrase occurs in Gen 22:17.

verses.zh: 利百加和她的使女们起来，骑上骆驼，跟着那仆人，仆人就带着利百加走了。
verses.en: Then Rebekah and her female servants mounted the camels and rode away with[NOTE:1] the man. So Abraham’s servant[NOTE:2] took Rebekah and left.
notes: Heb “And she arose, Rebekah and her female servants, and they rode upon camels and went after.”
Heb “the servant”; the word “Abraham’s” has been supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.

verses.zh: 那时，以撒住在南地，刚从庇耳・拉海・莱回来。
verses.en: Now[NOTE:1] Isaac came from[NOTE:2] Beer Lahai Roi,[NOTE:3] for[NOTE:4] he was living in the Negev.[NOTE:5]
notes: The disjunctive clause switches the audience’s attention to Isaac and signals a new episode in the story.
Heb “from the way of.”
The Hebrew name Beer Lahai Roi (בְּאֵר לַחַי רֹאִי, beʾer lakhay roʾi) means “The well of the Living One who sees me.” See Gen 16:14.
This disjunctive clause is explanatory.
Or “the South [country].”sn Negev is the name for the southern desert region in the land of Canaan.

verses.zh: 天将晚，以撒出来在田间默想，举目一看，见来了些骆驼。
verses.en: He[NOTE:1] went out to relax[NOTE:2] in the field in the early evening.[NOTE:3] Then he looked up[NOTE:4] and saw that[NOTE:5] there were camels approaching.
notes: Heb “Isaac”; the proper name has been replaced by the pronoun (“he”) in the translation for stylistic reasons.
The meaning of this Hebrew term is uncertain (cf. NASB, NIV “to meditate”; NRSV “to walk”).
Heb “at the turning of the evening.”
Heb “And he lifted up his eyes.” This idiom emphasizes the careful look Isaac had at the approaching caravan.
Heb “and look.” The clause introduced by the particle הִנֵּה (hinneh, “look”) invites the audience to view the scene through Isaac’s eyes.

verses.zh: 利百加举目看见以撒，就急忙下了骆驼，
verses.en: Rebekah looked up[NOTE:1] and saw Isaac. She got down from her camel
notes: Heb “lifted up her eyes.”

verses.zh: 问那仆人说：「这田间走来迎接我们的是谁？」仆人说：「是我的主人。」利百加就拿帕子蒙上脸。
verses.en: and asked[NOTE:1] Abraham’s servant,[NOTE:2] “Who is that man walking in the field toward us?” “That is my master,” the servant replied.[NOTE:3] So she took her veil and covered herself.
notes: Heb “and she said to.”
Heb “the servant.” The word “Abraham’s” has been supplied in the translation for clarity.
Heb “and the servant said.” The order of the introductory clause and the direct discourse has been rearranged in the translation for stylistic reasons.

verses.zh: 仆人就将所办的一切事都告诉以撒。
verses.en: The servant told Isaac everything that had happened.

verses.zh: 以撒便领利百加进了他母亲撒拉的帐棚，娶了她为妻，并且爱她。以撒自从他母亲不在了，这才得了安慰。
verses.en: Then Isaac brought Rebekah[NOTE:1] into his mother Sarah’s tent. He took her[NOTE:2] as his wife and loved her.[NOTE:3] So Isaac was comforted after his mother’s death.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “her”; the referent has been specified here in the translation for clarity.
Heb “Rebekah”; here the proper name was replaced by the pronoun (“her”) in the translation for stylistic reasons.
Heb “and he took Rebekah and she became his wife and he loved her.”
Heb “after his mother.” This must refer to Sarah’s death.
